ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Gwen Ifill — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: End of combination treatment: response CT, immune-related hypothyroidism, the first maintenance dostarlimab dose, and the survivorship plan

text.paragraph: End of combination treatment: CT result, thyroid tests, and the first maintenance dose. [S]

Ms. Ifill returns three weeks after her sixth and last cycle of combination treatment, all given on schedule. The CT a week ago shows no evidence of disease. Over the past month she has felt more tired than after earlier cycles, colder than usual, and a little slowed down, without low mood. The tingling in her toes is unchanged and does not affect walking. She has had no vaginal bleeding, pelvic pain, cough, breathlessness, diarrhea, rash, headache, dizziness or leg swelling. She saw Dr. Delacroix with the CT result and is ready to begin maintenance dostarlimab today. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2016-06-30; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well but tired; weight 72.4 kg; blood pressure 122/78, pulse 64, temperature 36.4 °C
No leg swelling; calf circumferences unchanged
Pinprick slightly reduced over the toes only; ankle reflexes present with a slow relaxation phase; steady gait

Postmenopausal bleeding for three weeks, about eight years after her last period, in a woman of 60 who takes no hormone therapy: endometrial cancer must be excluded. Office endometrial biopsy taken today, transvaginal ultrasound this week, and gynecologic oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem; no symptom of her real illness was made public. Superseded by the diagnosis at the gynecologic oncology consultation.

Endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, FIGO grade 2, mismatch repair deficient (loss of MLH1 and PMS2 staining), p53 wild-type pattern, on office endometrial biopsy, with enlarged right pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes on CT; surgical staging planned; synthetic modern detail linked to her publicly reported endometrial cancer
S — Synthetic histology, molecular result and extent; her family gave endometrial cancer as the cause of death (D), and nothing more about it was made public.

Metastatic endometrioid carcinoma in the right external iliac sentinel lymph node (9 mm deposit) and a left para-aortic lymph node (14 mm deposit), with the other nodes removed negative: FIGO 2013 stage IIIC2ii
S — Synthetic nodal disease found at surgical staging.
Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy from paclitaxel: tingling in the toes, grade 1 (sensory only, no effect on daily activities)
S — Synthetic common effect of paclitaxel.
Immune-related primary hypothyroidism from dostarlimab: TSH 11.8 with a low free T4, tiredness and feeling cold (grade 2)
S — Synthetic immune-related adverse event, among the most common with PD-1 inhibitors.

list.item:
Endometrioid endometrial cancer, stage IIIC2ii, MMRd, no evidence of disease after combination treatment (C54.1). No evidence of disease on CT, so radiation is not needed. Maintenance dostarlimab continues every six weeks for up to three years. Counts have recovered: hemoglobin 11.4 g/dL, neutrophils 2.8, platelets 228. Kidney and liver function and glucose are normal. Dr. Delacroix and she agreed today's plan. [S]
Dostarlimab 1000 mg today, then every six weeks.
Survivorship care plan given: examination with a pelvic examination every three months for two years; CT every six months for three years; no routine vaginal cytology and no CA-125.
Report vaginal bleeding, pelvic or abdominal pain, cough, weight loss or leg swelling.

Immune-related primary hypothyroidism, grade 2 (E03.2). TSH 11.8 with free T4 0.7, below range, and tiredness, feeling cold and a slower pulse: primary hypothyroidism from dostarlimab, the most common immune-related endocrine effect. Morning cortisol 13.1 is normal, so adrenal insufficiency is not the cause of her tiredness and thyroid replacement can start safely. Dostarlimab can continue with replacement. [S]
Levothyroxine 75 mcg daily before breakfast, starting today.
TSH and free T4 in six weeks, then with every dose.
Thyroid hormone will probably be needed long term.

Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, grade 1 (G62.0). Stable after the last paclitaxel; expected to improve slowly. [S]
Review at each visit.

list.item: Endometrial tissue diagnosis and ultrasound within one week, and a gynecologic oncology plan within three weeks of presentation. Outcome by 2016-01-20: Biopsy at the first visit, ultrasound in two days, result in four days, CT in eight, consultation at two weeks [S]
Surgical staging within four weeks of diagnosis. Outcome by 2016-02-24: Minimally invasive hysterectomy with sentinel node mapping and para-aortic node removal two weeks after the consultation [S]
Six cycles of dostarlimab with carboplatin and paclitaxel every three weeks without a delay of more than one week. Outcome by 2016-06-30: Six cycles on schedule; CT shows no evidence of disease [S]
Lynch syndrome tumor screening completed and explained before treatment starts. Outcome by 2016-02-24: MLH1 promoter hypermethylation found: acquired, not inherited; genetic counseling done [S]

Immune-related adverse events found early: TSH, liver tests, glucose and cortisol checked on schedule. Outcome by 2016-06-30: Hypothyroidism found on a scheduled TSH and treated without stopping dostarlimab; one missed baseline cortisol recorded and corrected [S]
PHQ-9 below 10 throughout treatment, with support she chooses. Outcome by 2016-06-30: PHQ-9 between 4 and 6 [S]
